claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

1. **Do you have any children you're responsible for?** If yes, how many children are there, and what are their ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 5 years old and lives here at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have a son named Alex who is 5 years old and lives with you at home.

Let me ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! And just to confirm:

**Are you the person responsible for Alex's care?** In other words, are you the one who looks after him day-to-day (providing things like food, clothes, and his general upkeep)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I look after him day-to-day - you know, all the usual things like his meals, clothes, and everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's actually part of why I'm asking. His other parent and I are both responsible for him, but we can't agree on who should claim the Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - that's a common situation. Thank you for being upfront about this.

Let me ask a couple more questions to give you complete information:

**Does Alex live with both of you, or does he primarily live with one of you? And if he splits time between homes, roughly how is that time divided?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex lives with me full-time at my home. He doesn't split time between homes - he just lives here with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Let me ask one more important question:

**Has Alex's other parent made a claim for Child Benefit for Alex, or are they planning to?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure if they've actually made a claim or not - that's part of the problem. We just haven't been able to agree between us who should be the one to claim it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining the situation. Let me ask a couple of final questions:

**Is Alex in any special circumstances, such as:**
- Currently in hospital or care?
- Receiving any benefits in his own name?
- In any kind of paid work?

(I'm assuming not since he's only 5, but I need to check to be thorough!)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. He's just a regular 5-year-old - he's not in hospital or care, doesn't get any benefits himself, and obviously he's too young to be working!

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that. Just one last question to complete my assessment:

**Do you have the right to reside in the UK?** For example, are you a UK citizen, do you have settled status, indefinite leave to remain, or another immigration status that gives you the right to live here?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have the right to live here in the UK.

## Assessment Complete: You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit

Good news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

### Here's why you're eligible:

✓ **Alex is 5 years old** - well under the age limit of 16 (or 20 if in approved education/training)  
✓ **You live in the UK** with the right to reside here  
✓ **You're responsible for Alex** - you provide his day-to-day care, food, clothes, and everything he needs  
✓ **Alex lives with you full-time** at your home  
✓ **No special circumstances** - Alex isn't in hospital, care, or receiving benefits in his own name

### About the disagreement with Alex's other parent:

The fact that you and Alex's other parent can't agree on who should claim doesn't make you ineligible. According to the rules, only one person can get Child Benefit for a child. If you both make claims for Alex, HMRC will decide who should receive it based on the circumstances.

Since Alex lives with you full-time and you provide all his day-to-day care, you have a strong case.

### What to do next:

You should go ahead and make a claim for Child Benefit. If the other parent also makes a claim, HMRC will help decide between you based on who is primarily responsible for Alex's care.
